newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ColMut says unlocated members may lose shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ColMut says unlocated members may lose shares.

text.p: Australian life office, the Colonial Mutual group, said on Wednesday that six to eight percent of its 538,000 members worldwide had not confirmed their addresses and might become ineligible for shares following the group's demutualisation.

"I think its six to eight percent of policyholders around the world haven't confirmed their details and they won't be sent shares unless they confirm," spokeman Simon Morgan told Reuters. But members had up to five years after the group's listing to confirm their address and claim the shares, Morgan said.

The unclaimed shares would be held in a trust account for five years after which dividends applying to half of the shares would be put toward "charitable works," while the remainder would be redistributed to existing shareholders, he said.
Colonial plans to distribute A$1.3 billion in shares to its members and raise another A$550 million, as part of its demutualisation and listing.
At meetings held in Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and Britain over the last two weeks, more than 36 percent of Colonial's members voted on the scheme with 97 percent of those in favour.
ColMut plans to list on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges in the second quarter of 1997, but must seek court approval on December 6 to end its 124-year-old mutual structure.
